summary: Round-1's destructive fixed-name fixture issue is fully eliminated. Both probes now use session-local TEMP tables, derive and match the actual temporary schema, and pass live PG19 NULL/visibility checks. The full tables/indexes query tests passed against live PostgreSQL 14-19 in a fresh disposable container, no probe objects remained after disconnect, and no new fixture, SQL-construction, diff/parser, credential, or evidence-safety risk was found.

verification.scope: Reviewed diff 6dd550e1916c2b9e6710057afae3cd18370d06e2..0ea45609269db10011b637e8ca8c80ef7b3976ff, with focused comparison against round-1 head 54a6473d8cb8a7d6f598a65bb781b1ea422d65b9. No product, frozen, or shared artifact was edited and no agents were spawned.

round1_finding_resolution.command: Source inspection and targeted pattern scan of internal/query/tables_test.go and indexes_test.go.
round1_finding_resolution.result: All anticipatory and deferred DROP TABLE statements are gone. tables_test.go:121 and indexes_test.go:117 use CREATE TEMP TABLE; indexes_test.go:119 creates the index on that temporary table. No persistent CREATE TABLE, DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER, GRANT, REVOKE, role change, or stats-reset operation remains in either test. Each test uses a fresh connection and defer conn.Close(), so fixed names are isolated per PostgreSQL session and temporary objects are removed by the server even if the client terminates abnormally.

temporary_identity.command: Source inspection of tables_test.go:123-125,147 and indexes_test.go:121-123,145.
temporary_identity.result: After creating the TEMP probe, each test resolves pg_my_temp_schema() through pg_namespace and matches the returned row using that actual schema plus the relation name (and index name for indexes). It does not assume public or a hardcoded pg_temp_N identifier.

live_tests.command: Started lesovsky/pgcenter-testing:0.0.11 as a uniquely named disposable container with only loopback port mappings, ran prepare-test-environment.sh inside it, then executed: go test ./internal/query/ -run 'StatTables|StatIndexes' -count=1 -v. A trap forcibly removed the container on exit.
live_tests.result: PASS in 1.358s. Test_StatTablesQueries and Test_StatIndexesQueries each passed live subtests for PostgreSQL 140000, 150000, 160000, 170000, 180000 and 190000. Test_StatTablesQuery_NullStatsAge and Test_StatIndexesQuery_NullStatsAge both ran and passed on PG19, proving temporary probes are visible in pg_stat_user_tables/pg_stat_user_indexes, correctly identified, and have blank NULL stats_age. All selector, query-source, column-order, template-residue, drain-error and diff-bound tests also passed. No live subtest was skipped in this disposable-fixture run.

side_effect_check.command: After the tests, query pg_class on PG19 for both probe table names and the probe index name across all namespaces; then verify the disposable container was removed and git status --short was empty.
side_effect_check.result: Probe object count was 0 after test connections closed. The disposable fixture container was removed, and the product worktree remained unchanged.

production_regression_check.command: git diff --exit-code 54a6473d8cb8a7d6f598a65bb781b1ea422d65b9..0ea45609269db10011b637e8ca8c80ef7b3976ff -- internal/query/tables.go internal/query/indexes.go; git diff --exit-code 6dd550e1916c2b9e6710057afae3cd18370d06e2..0ea45609269db10011b637e8ca8c80ef7b3976ff -- internal/query/functions.go internal/query/sizes.go; git diff --check 6dd550e1916c2b9e6710057afae3cd18370d06e2..0ea45609269db10011b637e8ca8c80ef7b3976ff
production_regression_check.result: All commands succeeded. Production query files did not change during the fix; functions.go and sizes.go remain untouched, and the complete diff passes whitespace validation.

sensitive_data_and_dependencies.command: Case-insensitive credential, private-key, token and PostgreSQL connection-string pattern scan limited to the four changed files; inspect dependency diff.
sensitive_data_and_dependencies.result: No sensitive-data matches or dependency changes. The report contains only sanitized test outcomes and no credentials, raw database rows, full archives, or terminal transcripts.
